security_audit.summary: The static alerts for backtick execution, path traversal, hidden-file access, hardcoded URLs, and reconnaissance are false positives caused by Markdown and documentation examples. The skill still presents shell interpolation, unpinned package installation, and third-party media disclosure risks. No prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.issue: CLI examples place user-authored JSON inside shell-quoted command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Pass arguments without a shell, or use a protected input file or standard input. Never interpolate user text into a shell command.

remediation.issue: The prerequisite installs an unpinned third-party CLI globally.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an audited CLI version and integrity value. Prefer a project-local installation with restricted permissions.

remediation.issue: Prompts and referenced media are processed by an external RunComfy service.
remediation.suggestion: Require user consent before submission. Warn against private or credential-bearing URLs and disclose remote retention policies.

semantic_findings.title: Shell Injection Risk in CLI Examples
semantic_findings.description: Examples place JSON containing user-authored prompts inside single-quoted shell arguments. An unescaped apostrophe can terminate quoting and permit injected shell commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: All three examples pass inline JSON through a shell command, and line 78 already requires manual apostrophe escaping. Safe behavior depends on reliable quoting not specified by the skill.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Global CLI Installation
semantic_findings.description: The prerequisite installs the latest third-party RunComfy CLI globally without a version or integrity pin. Package lifecycle code receives the installing user's permissions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 48 explicitly uses a global npm install with no version. This creates a clear supply-chain exposure even without evidence that the current package is malicious.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party Media and Prompt Disclosure
semantic_findings.description: The workflow submits prompts and media URLs to RunComfy, whose servers fetch referenced content. Private media or signed URL credentials may leave the user's trust boundary.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly states that the CLI posts inputs to the Model API and that remote model servers fetch supplied URLs. The privacy impact follows directly from that workflow.

content.user_title: Animate Still Images with RunComfy Models
content.value_statement: Choosing the wrong image-to-video model wastes time and generation credits. This skill routes each request to a suitable RunComfy model and supplies model-specific inputs.
actual_capabilities: Routes general animation requests to HappyHorse 1.0 I2V.
Routes custom voiceover and lip-sync requests to Wan 2.7.
Routes combined image, video, and audio references to Seedance 2.0 Pro.
Provides model-specific prompt, duration, resolution, and aspect-ratio guidance.
Provides RunComfy CLI invocation patterns for each supported route.
Explains exit codes, authentication, output downloads, and model limits.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, an account, network access, and valid authentication.
Sends prompts and referenced media to an external model service.
Selects one model per call and does not blend routes or stitch clips.
Each route has model-specific duration, resolution, format, and aspect-ratio limits.

use_cases.title: Animate a Product Still
use_cases.description: Create a short product reveal while preserving packaging geometry, logo placement, and the original image aspect.

use_cases.title: Produce Localized Talking Heads
use_cases.description: Generate repeated talking-head clips by changing the voiceover audio while keeping visual settings and seed consistent.

use_cases.title: Combine Multimodal References
use_cases.description: Create one clip using a subject image, camera movement from video, and voice tone from audio.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Portrait
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate [image URL] as a five-second portrait clip. Keep the face stable. Add subtle breathing, one blink, and a slow camera push-in.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner portrait animation with one clear motion beat.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Product Reveal
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a product reveal from [image URL]. Preserve packaging and logo geometry. Use one slow orbit, controlled highlights, 1080P, and eight seconds.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate product animation with preservation requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Lip-Sync a Voiceover
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a vertical talking-head clip using [audio URL]. Match the clip duration to the audio. Use warm studio lighting and avoid subtitles or flicker.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced voiceover-driven lip-sync for a vertical video.

prompt_templates.title: Direct a Multimodal Scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Combine [subject image], [reference video], and [reference audio]. Keep the subject identity, follow the reference camera movement, and match the voice tone. Produce an eight-second 9:16 clip with synchronized audio.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced composition using image, video, and audio references.

output_examples.input: Animate this portrait with subtle movement and a slow camera push-in.
output: Selected HappyHorse 1.0 I2V for identity-preserving portrait animation.
Prepared a five-second motion prompt with the source aspect ratio.
Requested the generated video in the chosen output directory.

output_examples.input: Create a vertical spokesperson clip that follows my twelve-second voiceover.
output: Selected Wan 2.7 because the request includes custom lip-sync audio.
Matched the video duration to twelve seconds and selected 9:16 framing.
Added visual guidance for stable framing, warm light, and no subtitles.

output_examples.input: Use my portrait, reference camera clip, and voice sample in one scene.
output: Selected Seedance 2.0 Pro for combined image, video, and audio references.
Numbered each reference so the prompt assigns identity, movement, and voice correctly.
Prepared an eight-second clip with synchronized audio.

best_practices: Use media URLs you are authorized to share with RunComfy.
Describe one primary motion beat and state the visual details that must remain stable.
Match clip duration to reference audio and reuse seeds when comparing variants.
anti_patterns: Do not place credentials, private tokens, or unnecessary personal data in media URLs or prompts.
Do not request multiple model routes in one call because the skill selects only one route.
Do not combine reference media with conflicting subjects, camera styles, or visual aesthetics.

faq.question: What do I need before using this skill?
faq.answer: Install the RunComfy CLI, sign in, and provide accessible media URLs that meet the selected model requirements.

faq.question: How does the skill choose a model?
faq.answer: It uses HappyHorse for general animation, Wan for custom voiceover lip-sync, and Seedance for combined image, video, and audio references.

faq.question: Can I use my own voiceover?
faq.answer: Yes. The Wan route accepts WAV or MP3 audio and uses it to drive lip-sync.

faq.question: Can I choose a different output aspect ratio?
faq.answer: Wan and Seedance support listed aspect ratios. HappyHorse keeps the source image aspect ratio.

faq.question: Where is the generated video saved?
faq.answer: The RunComfy CLI downloads generated output to the directory selected for the command.

faq.question: What data leaves my device?
faq.answer: Prompts and media URLs reach RunComfy services. Remote model servers fetch the referenced media for processing.
